findings: src/optimizer/deliminator.cpp:87-93: the new condition depends only on structure: the join type (SEMI/ANTI) and whether the RHS subtree contains a blocking or dedup operator. It matches no tables, columns, literals or sizes. It applies to any correlated EXISTS/NOT EXISTS over a filtered outer table, which is a common analytical pattern.

Correctness: when the condition holds, the code takes the same removal path that already runs whenever the LHS has no selection. RemoveJoinWithDelimGet still checks whether each join can be removed (equality conditions and NULL handling), and the delim join is only turned into a comparison join if every join was removed. The previous heuristic was about performance only, not correctness, so this does not add a new risk of wrong results for NULLs, ANTI joins or IS NOT DISTINCT FROM.

HasBlockingOperator does not list set operations (union/except/intersect) or CTE materialisation. Missing them can only cost performance (the delim join would not be kept), never correctness, so this is acceptable for a heuristic.
No changes to tests, settings, timing or other files. The change is small and has a single purpose.
